title: Salt Security — AEO & Structured-Data Review
description: Independent answer-engine and structured-data review of salt.security by Mousa Batarseh — 57 of 60 pages without JSON-LD, no FAQPage, llms.txt 404 and 720 disallowed sitemap URLs. For the Website Manager role.

blocks.text: SEC. 01 — OVERVIEW · FOR THE WEBSITE MANAGER ROLE
Found by people. Quoted by machines.

Salt is repositioning around agentic security and answer engines — but its pages give machines nothing to quote. 57 of 60 sampled pages carry no structured data. There's no FAQPage anywhere, even where the H2s are questions. llms.txt is a 404. And the sitemap submits 720 URLs that robots.txt disallows. Here's the answer layer I'd build in Webflow.
FAQPage blocks — even on question-form H2s
The homepage (Corporation) and blog posts (BlogPosting) carry schema. /platform, /demo-request, every use-case and comparison page don't.
/api-security-101 already asks and answers in H2s. Wrapped in FAQPage, it becomes something an answer engine can lift.
2,929 sitemap URLs, 720 of them under disallowed paths; 32 noindex customer stubs; titles still say “API Security.”
Independent — not affiliated with Salt Security
